title: flexibility of isolated lumbar discs (anterior column units) about principal and combined moment axes
condition: anterior column unit (posterior elements removed), no preload

quantity.name: flexibility
quantity.definition: slope of the most linear (best-fit, 6 points) high-flexibility portion of the rotation-moment curve; mean ± SD (experimental values only)

source.authors: Spenciner D, Greene D, Paiva J, Palumbo M, Crisco J
source.sample: 7 lumbar anterior column units (4 L2-L3, 3 L4-L5) from 4 spines; human cadaver ACUs: posterior elements removed by bilateral pedicle transection, ALL and PLL intact; disc grade (Thompson) 1.9-3.7

protocol.summary: ACUs potted (urethane) to mid-vertebral body, disc mid-transverse plane perpendicular to the vertical axis. Pure unconstrained moments 0 ± 8 Nm, sinusoidal 0.1 Hz, about 3 principal and 10 combined axes (servohydraulic frame + universal joints + linear bearing tables; off-axis moments < 4%); 4 preconditioning cycles, 5th cycle analysed; initial axis pair re-tested at the end and averaged. No axial compressive force applied (stated in Discussion). Coordinate origin at mid-sagittal/mid-transverse disc planes, 2/3 disc depth posterior to the anterior wall.
how_to_simulate: Model a lumbar disc-only unit (both vertebral bodies, disc, ALL, PLL; no posterior elements); fix the inferior body
Apply pure moments of ±8 Nm (no preload) about the flexion-extension, lateral bending and axial rotation axes and the listed combined axes (vector sums of unit principal axes)

Report per direction: ROM = rotation about the moment axis at 8 Nm; flexibility = steepest linear slope (deg/Nm); NZ = rotation-axis intercept of that tangent line (extrapolated, not the zero-load laxity)
protocol.notes: NZ here = intercept of the high-flexibility tangent with the rotation axis (Fig 3), not the Wilke zero-load NZ. Levels pooled (L2-L3 and L4-L5). ROM is one direction from neutral. Testing order effect: ROM +1.4 deg and NZ +1.1 deg between first and last test of the same axis.
